story_type: space station damaged at launch, overheating, crew flies up with a homemade sunshade, 1973
hook: A minute after launch, the space station lost its shield.
narration: About a minute after launch, America's first space station lost its shield.
This was Skylab, launched with no one aboard on May fourteenth, 1973.
Clouds hid it from the tracking cameras. Telemetry showed the meteoroid shield had come out early, and a solar wing was sending almost no power.
In the first orbit, the temperature inside started rising fast.
In space there is no air to carry heat away, so a sunlit wall just keeps getting hotter.
The crew launch went on indefinite hold. The whole Skylab program was at stake.
Engineers built and tested emergency sunshades, and picked a folding parasol.
Eleven days after Skylab, Pete Conrad's crew flew up and circled it. Where the shield should be was bare gold.
[short pause] From inside, they pushed the parasol out through a small science airlock. It took about four hours.
outcome: Under the parasol, the temperature inside Skylab settled in the mid seventies.

title: Space station lost its shield at launch
description:
Skylab launched without a crew on May 14, 1973, and lost its meteoroid shield about a minute into flight. With the workshop overheating, the first crew launched 11 days later and deployed a parasol sunshade from inside. From the 1973 NASA film Skylab: The First 40 Days.
